## Summary

I investigated ticket T-2009 and identified the root cause: the pricing-engine pods are crashing due to an **application bug**, not a Kubernetes issue. The pod logs reveal a panic in the pricing-engine's rule compiler when it attempts to process a new pricing rule called "BF-2026-STACKED" that has 3 tiers with stacking enabled. The bug is an array index out-of-bounds error in `/src/internal/rules/tiers.go:88`. 

Since the rules-admin pod is running and serving 1,204 active rules (revision 8841), someone has added new rules that trigger this latent bug in the application code. The CrashLoopBackOff status is Kubernetes behaving correctly by attempting to restart the failing containers.

The fix requires either updating the pricing-engine application to handle this tier configuration correctly, or modifying/removing the problematic rule from rules-admin.
